conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
$S_N1$ vs $S_N2$ REACTION PROFILES
                       
   $S_N1$ MECHANISM (Two Steps via Carbocation):
   Step 1 (RDS): $\text{R-X} \xrightarrow{\text{Slow}} \mathbf{\text{R}^+ \text{ (Carbocation)}} + \text{X}^-$
   Step 2 (Fast): $\text{R}^+ + \text{Nu}^- \xrightarrow{\text{Fast}} \text{R-Nu} \quad \implies \mathbf{\text{Rate} = k [\text{R-X}]}
   
   $S_N2$ MECHANISM (Concerted One Step via Transition State):
   $\text{Nu}^- + \text{R-X} \longrightarrow [\text{Nu}\cdots\text{C}\cdots\text{X}]^\ddagger \longrightarrow \mathbf{\text{Nu-R} + \text{X}^-} \quad \implies \mathbf{\text{Rate} = k [\text{R-X}] [\text{Nu}^-]}

                      $S_N2$ WALDEN INVERSION TRANSITION STATE
                      
                         H                     H
                         │                     │
   Nu⁻ ──►  C ── X  ──►  Nu ⋯ C ⋯ X  ──►  Nu ─ C   +  X⁻
           / \           │  / \                / \
          H   H          H H   H              H   H
     (Initial)       (5-Coordinate TBP)   (**100% Inversion**)
conceptBreakdown.content: Nucleophilic substitution in haloalkanes proceeds via two distinct mechanical pathways: Unimolecular ($S_N1$) and Bimolecular ($S_N2$).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
S_N1 vs S_N2 COMPARISON MATRIX

1. Kinetics:        S_N1: 1st Order (Rate = k[R-X])       | S_N2: 2nd Order (Rate = k[R-X][Nu⁻])
2. Steps:           S_N1: 2 Steps (Carbocation R⁺)        | S_N2: 1 Concerted Step (TBP X‡)
3. Substrate Order: S_N1: 3° > 2° > 1° (Carbocation stab) | S_N2: CH₃X > 1° > 2° > 3° (Steric)
4. Stereochemistry: S_N1: Racemization (partial inversion)| S_N2: 100% Complete Walden Inversion
5. Nucleophile:     S_N1: Rate independent of [Nu⁻]       | S_N2: Rate proportional to [Nu⁻] strength
6. Optimal Solvent: S_N1: Polar Protic (H₂O, EtOH)        | S_N2: Polar Aprotic (DMSO, DMF, Acetone)
7. Leaving Group:   I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ >> F⁻ in both mechanisms
conceptBreakdown.content: Review the full 8-parameter comparison between $S_N1$ and $S_N2$ pathways including steric hindrance (neopentyl bromide is inert to $S_N2$) and carbocation stability (allyl and benzyl halides react rapidly via $S_N1$).

quickRevision: S_N1: Rate = k[R-X], two steps, carbocation, 3° > 2° > 1°, polar protic solvents, racemization.
S_N2: Rate = k[R-X][Nu⁻], one step, TBP transition state, CH₃X > 1° > 2° > 3°, polar aprotic solvents, 100% Walden inversion.
Neopentyl bromide (1°) is extremely inert to S_N2 due to bulky t-butyl steric hindrance.
Allyl and benzyl halides undergo rapid S_N1 due to resonance-stabilized carbocations.
Leaving group ability: I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ >> F⁻.
